item.stem:
[Image: Graph of y = x + cos x]

Sophia is studying the graph of the function y = x + cos x shown above. She says that the slope at point A is the same as the slope at point B. Explain why she is correct.

descriptors: Explanation involving differentiating and showing the gradient is the same at x = π and x = 2π; or using the nature of the cosine function to establish that the gradient is the same at x = π and x = 2π
Correct answer using calculator with adequate explanation
Calculator used—answer incorrect or explanation inadequate
Differentiates correctly but does not give adequate explanation of why slopes are equal
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

item.figure_description: A Cartesian coordinate plane with horizontal axis labeled x and vertical axis labeled y, intersecting at the origin labeled O. The grid lines correspond to labels on the axes. The x-axis is labeled at -π, O (0), π, 2π, and 3π. The y-axis is labeled at -4, 4, and 8. The graph of the curve y = x + cos x is shown passing through the grid from x < -π to x > 3π. Two points on the curve are marked with solid black dots and labeled: point A at x = π and point B at x = 2π.
item.calibration: Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it.
